Question_text: A student investigates the motion of a toy car down a ramp. The toy car is released from rest on the ramp at position 1, as shown in Fig. 1.1.
image: A diagram labelled Fig. 1.1 (not to scale) shows a toy car on a ramp. The ramp starts at 'position 1' at a higher elevation. The toy car is shown at the top of the ramp. The ramp leads down to a horizontal 'floor'. 'position 2' is indicated at the point where the ramp meets the floor. 'position 3' is further along the floor where the car comes to rest. The horizontal distance between 'position 2' and 'position 3' is labelled 'd'. A vertical height 'h' is also indicated between position 1 and position 2, to be marked by the student as per part (a)(iii).

Parts.part_text: Suggest a method for measuring d.
Describe how the student ensures that the toy car is released from the same point on the ramp each time.
On Fig. 1.1, mark the height h through which the toy car falls from position 1 to position 2.
The student releases the toy car from the same point on the ramp five times and measures d each time. The student obtains the following values of d in centimetres. 180 179 171 172 174
Calculate dav, the average value for d. Give your answer to a suitable number of significant figures.
Suggest a reason why the results for d vary.

By adjusting the angle of the ramp, the student repeats the experiment for different values of the height h. The results obtained for h and dav are recorded in Fig. 1.2. Fig. 1.2 is a table showing two columns: 'h/cm' with values 22, 20, 18, 16, 14, 12, 10; and 'dav/cm' with corresponding values 124, 109, 94, 84, 70, 55, 44.
On Fig. 1.3, plot the graph of dav/cm on the y-axis against h/cm on the x-axis. Draw the line of best fit.
Parts.image: An empty Cartesian graph grid labelled Fig. 1.3, with '0' at the origin. The y-axis is intended for 'dav/cm' and the x-axis for 'h/cm', and is to be used for plotting the given data and drawing a line of best fit.

Parts.part_text: Describe the relationship between dav and h.
The car is now released with h = 2cm. Use your graph to state what happens to the car.

Question_text: A student investigates the effect of a converging lens on light from the Sun. The student uses a converging lens to produce a clear image of the Sun on a piece of white card, as shown in Fig. 2.1.
image: A diagram labelled Fig. 2.1 (not to scale) illustrates a converging lens experiment. Parallel rays of 'light from a point on the Sun' enter from the left. They pass through a 'converging lens' (represented by a biconvex lens symbol) and converge to form an 'image of the point on the Sun' on a 'white card' placed to the right of the lens. A distance 's' is to be marked on the diagram, representing the distance from the center of the lens to the image on the card.

Parts.part_text: On Fig. 2.1, mark this distance and label it s.
State the name given to this distance.
Describe in detail the experimental techniques used to obtain an accurate value for this distance.

Question_text: Three resistors A, B and C are connected in a circuit with a cell, as shown in Fig. 3.1.
image: A circuit diagram labelled Fig. 3.1 shows a cell (battery symbol) connected to three resistors. Resistor A is in series with a parallel combination of resistors B and C. The cell is on the left. Resistor A is positioned on the top branch. Resistors B and C are connected in parallel to each other, forming a branch on the right side of the circuit, connected to the cell via resistor A.

Parts.part_text: State the arrangement of resistors B and C in the circuit.
On Fig. 3.1, draw
the symbol for a voltmeter to measure the voltage provided by the cell,
an X to indicate the position of an ammeter to measure the current in resistor A.
The voltmeter is shown in Fig. 3.2.
Parts.image: A diagram labelled Fig. 3.2 shows an analog voltmeter. It has a circular dial with a scale from 0 to 10 V, marked with major divisions at each whole number and ten subdivisions between each major mark. The needle points exactly to the 5V mark. The voltmeter also shows positive (+) and negative (-) terminals.

Parts.part_text: State the voltmeter reading V on Fig. 3.2.

Resistors A, B and C have resistances R_A, R_B and R_C where R_A = R_B = R_C = 10Ω. Use your answer for V in (c)(i) and the relationship below to find the value of the current I in resistor A. I = V / (R_A + (R_C * R_B) / (R_C + R_B))

Four students try to build the circuit of Fig. 3.1 with three 10Ω resistors and a cell. Their circuit diagrams are shown in Fig. 3.3. State and explain which circuit is not the same as the circuit in Fig. 3.1.
Parts.image:
A diagram labelled Fig. 3.3 shows four different circuit diagrams, each containing a cell and three resistors.
Circuit 1 shows all three resistors connected in series with the cell.
Circuit 2 shows one resistor in series with a parallel combination of the other two resistors. This configuration matches Fig. 3.1.
Circuit 3 shows one resistor in series with a parallel combination of the other two resistors. This configuration also matches Fig. 3.1, drawn with the parallel branch on the bottom instead of the right.
Circuit 4 shows all three resistors connected in parallel with the cell.

Question_text: The effect of surface colour on the cooling of an object is investigated. Fig. 4.1 shows two sets of apparatus used in this investigation.
image: A diagram labelled Fig. 4.1 shows two experimental setups to investigate cooling. Both setups consist of a test-tube containing 'hot water' with a 'thermometer' immersed in it. The left setup, 'test-tube A', has a 'dull black outer surface'. The right setup, 'test-tube B', has a 'shiny silver outer surface'. Both setups are otherwise identical.

Parts.part_text: State two factors that must be the same for the two sets of apparatus so that the cooling curves may be compared.
On Fig. 4.2, write the headings in the table that is to be used to record the results for test-tube A.
Parts.image: An empty table with two columns, labelled Fig. 4.2, provided for recording experimental results. The table is blank, implying that the student needs to add appropriate headings such as 'Time / s' and 'Temperature / °C'.

Parts.part_text: On Fig. 4.3, sketch and label the shape of the cooling curves for test-tube A and for test-tube B.
Parts.image: An empty Cartesian graph grid labelled Fig. 4.3, with '0' at the origin for both axes. The x-axis is typically for time and the y-axis for temperature, intended for sketching and labelling cooling curves for both test-tube A and test-tube B.
